citation: P. B. Greene, 'Water Works', stereograph, [Chicago: P. B. Greene, 1871]. Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, LC-DIG-stereo-1s12375.
author: P. B. Greene, photographer and publisher (the card's mount)
date: [October-December 1871] (after the fire: the works stand roofless)
describes_date: 1871, just after the fire of 8-9 October
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division (STEREO U.S. GEOG FILE - Illinois--Chicago--Fire, 1871). The left half of the card is committed at data/sources/assets/landmarks_1871_t3689/loc_1s12375_water_tower_left.jpg.
locator: The left half of the card: the Water Tower from the burnt ground to the west, its west front face-on, the works' long front on Pine Street behind it at left with the centre pavilion and the smoke-stack, a fenced lot and a street in the foreground, sheds and ruins at right.
rights_note: The Library of Congress: 'No known restrictions on publication.' A photograph published in 1871.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-20 (T-3689) from the Library's master TIFF of the whole card (tile.loc.gov storage-services, service/pnp/stereo/1s12000/1s12300/1s12375); the left half cropped and committed at 1600 x 1662 px, sha256 fa813beebf89ee89bff37f9735d5cedbeb04fd8650f1c3501b88fca1ef94308d.
note: The Water Tower and the works after the fire, a few weeks after 9 October 1871. Monochrome.
what_it_supplies: the tower's massing and heights as they stood in 1871
the works' long front, pavilion, corner turrets and stack, and where they stand behind the tower
what_it_does_not_supply: the works' south half (behind the tower)
